answer: Photorefractive bismuth silicon oxide holography anchors agents to unique optical media. Each node modulates a 532 nm laser to write dynamic volume gratings into a raw BSO crystal; it reads diffraction phase patterns across an umber interference field; finally, it submits signed 2D fringe proofs to network peers. Simulating 10,000 identities requires maintaining concurrent optical volumes costing 4.8 million dollars in custom spatial light modulators and 320 megawatts of laser power. Emulating this phase orchard resembles stabilizing an entire dune against desert squalls.
